report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Probe construction and checking for arrival, instruction, anchoring, comprehension; probe registry.

symbols.name: _SUMMARY_DECOYS
symbols.note: Tuple of 8 decoy summary strings, each a plausible one-line file summary.

symbols.name: _SUMMARY_TARGETS
symbols.note: Tuple of 3 summary strings, each mentioning 'rollback'.

symbols.name: _filler
symbols.note: Generates 'lines' lines of padding, each with 12 words chosen from _FILLER_WORDS via rng.

symbols.name: ARRIVAL_PAD_LINES
symbols.note: 40: pad lines for arrival probe.

symbols.name: build_arrival
symbols.note: Builds prompt with NONCE-<nonce> first line, filler, instructions, TAILWORD: <word> last line.

symbols.name: expect_arrival
symbols.note: Returns 'NONCE-<nonce> <word>' where word is rng-chosen from _TAIL_WORDS.

symbols.name: check_arrival
symbols.note: Checks reply contains both NONCE-<nonce> and tail word (case-insensitive, word boundary). Returns (bool, reason).

symbols.name: _FENCE_RE
symbols.note: Regex matching leading/trailing code fences.

symbols.name: build_instruction
symbols.note: Builds prompt requiring exactly 'OK-<nonce>'.

symbols.name: expect_instruction
symbols.note: Returns 'OK-<nonce>'.

symbols.name: _normalise
symbols.note: Strips code fences, surrounding quotes, whitespace, trailing period.

symbols.name: check_instruction
symbols.note: Checks reply equals 'OK-<nonce>' exactly; if contains it but not exact, returns not_exact; else answer_absent.

symbols.name: _anchor_pair
symbols.note: Returns (body, decoy, correct) for one nonce: picks two sets from _ANCHOR_SETS, picks decoy from prior and correct from new.

symbols.name: build_anchoring
symbols.note: Returns prompt body from _anchor_pair.

symbols.name: expect_anchoring
symbols.note: Returns correct word from _anchor_pair.

symbols.name: check_anchoring
symbols.note: Checks reply: if decoy present returns anchored_on_decoy; else if correct present returns True; else wrong_word.

symbols.name: _NUMBER_WORDS
symbols.note: Maps 'one','two','three' to 1,2,3.

symbols.name: _NUMBER_RE
symbols.note: Regex matching digits 1-3 or words one/two/three, case-insensitive.

symbols.name: _summaries
symbols.note: Returns (list of 3 summary lines, target number 1-3). Picks 3 decoys, replaces one with a rollback target.

symbols.name: build_comprehension
symbols.note: Builds prompt listing three numbered summaries, asks which mentions rollback, answer with number.

symbols.name: expect_comprehension
symbols.note: Returns target as string.

symbols.name: check_comprehension
symbols.note: Extracts number from reply, compares to target. Returns no_number, wrong_number, or True.

symbols.name: ProbeSpec
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with name, severity, build, check, expect, blurb. Validates severity in SEVERITIES.

symbols.name: PROBES
symbols.note: Tuple of ProbeSpec for arrival and instruction (and anchoring, but truncated in this chunk).

claims.text: Requiring BOTH tokens back is what makes a single cheap probe cover both.
claims.why: check_arrival requires both head (NONCE-<nonce>) and tail word present; if either missing returns failure.

claims.text: a model that lost the tail may still echo the head token while complaining about the cut, and that reply is correctly rejected because it cannot contain a tail word it never received.
claims.why: If tail missing, tail_ok False, so check returns tailword_absent even if head present.

claims.text: Accept only if BOTH ends of the prompt demonstrably arrived.
claims.why: It requires head_ok and tail_ok both true; otherwise returns failure.

claims.text: Strip TRANSPORT artefacts only -- never content.
claims.why: It strips whitespace, code fences, surrounding quotes, trailing period; no other content removal.

claims.text: Anything the model actually chose to say survives this and is judged.
claims.why: Only strips the listed artefacts; remaining text is compared exactly.

claims.text: It knew the answer and said more anyway. That is the degradation this probe exists for -- a lane that is alive and no longer obedient.
claims.why: If want is in reply but not exact, returns 'not_exact', distinguishing from 'answer_absent'.

claims.text: Detect a lane that copied the decoy instead of answering.
Reported as a QUALITY signal by :data:`PROBES`: a model anchoring on a prior turn is alive, reachable and useless for reasoning work.
claims.why: The PROBES registry is defined later in this chunk but its full contents and severity assignments are not visible; the anchoring probe's severity is not shown here.

claims.text: Calling that a liveness failure would page someone about a model choice; calling it nothing is how it went unnoticed for a day.
claims.why: This is a historical/anecdotal claim not testable from code.

claims.text: Decoy present WINS over a correct word also being present: a reply containing both is a reply that regurgitated the transcript.
claims.why: The code checks has_decoy first and returns anchored_on_decoy regardless of has_correct.

claims.text: The nonce is deliberately NOT in this prompt: the answer is a digit, and a nonce full of digits would give a lazy checker something to trip over.
claims.why: The prompt text does not include nonce; only summaries and instruction.

claims.text: Exactly one of them mentions a rollback. Which one?
claims.why: _summaries replaces exactly one of three decoy lines with a rollback target; the other two are decoys that do not mention rollback per the decoy list.

observations.what: _summaries uses rng.sample(_SUMMARY_DECOYS, 3) which picks 3 distinct decoys; then replaces one with a rollback target. This guarantees exactly one rollback line only if none of the decoys mention rollback; the decoy strings do not contain the word 'rollback' (checked: 'parses a config file and reports unknown keys', etc.), so the claim holds.

check_arrival uses re.search with word boundary for tail word; if tail word is a substring of a longer word, it would not match, but tail words are chosen from _TAIL_WORDS (not visible) and are likely standalone. The head token check is a plain substring, so a reply containing 'NONCE-<nonce>' as part of a longer string would pass.

check_comprehension extracts the first number found; if the reply contains multiple numbers, it uses the first. The prompt asks for just its number, so a reply with multiple numbers would be judged by the first. This is a potential ambiguity but not a defect in the probe as designed.

_normalise strips a trailing period unconditionally; if the model's exact answer ends with a period as part of the content (e.g., 'OK-abc.'), it would be stripped and pass. This is a deliberate tolerance, but could mask a model adding a period.
The chunk ends mid-PROBES definition; anchoring and comprehension probes are not fully shown. The claims about PROBES registry severity are uncheckable from this chunk.

risks: _summaries | low | Guarantee of exactly one rollback depends on decoys not containing 'rollback'; verified in this chunk, but if decoys change, the probe breaks silently | Check _SUMMARY_DECOYS for absence of 'rollback'

check_arrival | low | Head token check is substring, not word-bounded; a reply with 'NONCE-abc' inside a longer token would pass | Confirm _TAIL_WORDS and head token format do not overlap with other text
check_comprehension | low | First number found is used; a reply with multiple numbers could be misjudged | Confirm prompt strongly discourages extra numbers
_normalise | low | Trailing period stripped could mask a model adding a period | Decide if that is acceptable tolerance
